design:
EXECUTION-ONLY SELF-LEARNING LOOP over a pre-decided daily trade list (the parent book — 819 trend today, whatever passes TASK_915 later — supplies the orders; the loop never chooses direction or size).

Episode = one order (asset, side, quantity fixed by the parent) with a hard deadline T in {15, 30, 60} min after the daily rebalance time. State = private (time-left, inventory-left; Nevmyvaka's factorization) + market (spread in ticks, top-of-book imbalance, last-5-min |return|/vol, hour-of-day, 907's frozen-mid flag — all available from the 907 recorder's book(depth 10)+trade feed, `experiments/907_live_fill_probe/recorder.py:103,175`). Action each minute = {post-only at touch, post-only 1 tick behind, join+cross remainder, cancel/replace}; at T any remainder is crossed at market — MANDATORY terminal execution, so abstention is not in the action set. Reward = −implementation shortfall vs the decision mid, fees included (maker/taker per the operator's actual Kraken tier), realized within ≤60 min of each order. Learner = exact backward-induction over (T×I×L) as in Nevmyvaka–Feng–Kearns 2006, or a contextual bandit over rule parameters (deadline, offset); NOT MuZero — a ≤60-step, 2–4-action horizon with known inventory dynamics needs no tree, and the memo's §2 argument (search over known inventory dynamics adds nothing) applies here too. Training data = REAL micro-notional post-only orders (D65 phase 2 rails, `phase2_rails.py`; venue minimums ~$5–10), not a simulator: the fill event exists only for an order in the queue (`PREREGISTRATION.md:44-64` "a touch is not a fill"). Deployable artifact = (a) a measured cost tier (fee_maker + realized adverse selection + non-fill×taker) that replaces the assumed fee16/slip5, and (b) a two-line rule or a small table — never a checkpoint.

Why this is the ONE controlled MDP available: the price path is exogenous to a daily book (memo §2), but a resting limit's fill IS caused by the agent's own price/time choice (queue position → fill probability → adverse selection). Nevmyvaka's independence trick — market variables evolve independently of a small order, private variables are fully controlled — holds almost exactly at micro size on BTC/ETH books. Why it cannot create drift: the parent fixes the trade list, so E[return] of the book is fixed by the parent's forecast; execution changes only realized cost (and adds tracking error when unfilled). It is a whisper about COST, not direction.

Hardware actually needed: CPU only (learner is a table/ridge; recorder already runs under safe_run on gpu-server). The 907 capture reader peaks at 14.8 GB RSS (TASK_914 fixes). Zero GPU; the 64 GB GPUs are irrelevant to every part of this.
what_the_loop_learns: Learned object = the queue-value surface: P(fill | offset, time-left, spread, imbalance, vol, hour) × E[adverse markout | fill, same state] − E[cost of crossing the remainder at deadline | state]. A direct estimator (a per-state average of realized shortfall, or 907's touch-conditional markout deciles) gives the SAME quantity once the state grid is fixed — the "loop" adds only (i) the private-variable DP (when to give up passivity as time runs out; Nevmyvaka Fig. 4: aggressive as inventory remains and time runs out) and (ii) on-policy data collection from real fills. Beyond a static rule ("post-only at touch, cross at T"), the literature's measured increment is: Nevmyvaka +27–35% over OPTIMIZED submit-and-leave with private vars, ~50% with market vars, on 5–10k-share institutional orders where impact dominates; Ning et al. 0–12 bp of TWAP P&L, nil on 2/9 stocks; Digital Finance 2023 on Kraken BTC/USD gets a 60% cut (26 → 10.1 bp) with a STATIC kernel and no learning — the crypto saving is fee-structure-driven, not impact-driven. Why the surface exists in this venue's data: Kraken BTC/USD mid is frozen 46.5% of minutes (real stillness, run-50 falsification) and ETH freezes when locked at a 1-tick spread — fill probability at the touch is strongly state-dependent (frozen vs moving), which is exactly what a state-conditional rule can exploit and a flat model cannot. What it is NOT: it carries zero conditional-mean information about the parent's return; it is a cost-tier estimator with a controller attached.
worth_if_ic_is_zero: Arithmetic on the record's own book: turnover 0.1551/day (`trader/backtest.py:455-462`), cost = turnover × c one-sided (`trader/backtest.py:188-190`; `POWERED_RESULT.md:7`), so c bp/side costs 56.6·c bp/yr: 21 bp = 11.9%/yr = the measured 0.18 Sharpe (gross +0.74 → net@21 +0.56, `POWERED_RESULT.md` FULL row), implying book vol ≈ 66%/yr. Cutting realized cost 21 → 12 bp = +5.1%/yr = +0.077 Sharpe; 21 → 8 bp = +7.4%/yr = +0.11 Sharpe (range +0.06..+0.12 at 60–80% vol). The entire stack to zero is +0.18. If the parent's IC ≈ 0 (gross Sharpe ≈ 0, which is the 2024–26 trend read: net@8 2024 +0.041, 2026H1 −1.659, LEDGER `898/trend-decay`), the loop moves net from ≈ −0.18 toward ≈ −0.07: it cannot cross zero, cannot make a book BEAR-positive, and cannot move the PIT +0.56 CI[−0.13,+1.23] to exclude 0 (+0.11 shifts the point to +0.67 inside a ±0.68 interval). The +0.97 bar is unreachable from +0.74 gross even at zero cost. Worth at IC≈0: zero as edge; positive only as infrastructure — a measured cost tier for any book that later passes 915, the live-execution module for gate ladder rungs 3–4 (`docs/findings/deployment_gate_ladder.md`), and closure of the never-validated maker-fill model (D65). Of the ≤0.11 ceiling, the fee half (~10–12 bp/side maker-vs-taker at the same Kraken tier, or 0–8 bp if the operator's attainable maker fee is really 8–16 bp as recorded in TASK_897:284) is a schedule lookup captured by a two-line rule; the LEARNED increment over that rule is plausibly 1–4 bp/side = +0.01..+0.035 Sharpe.
measured_failure_mode_and_escape: Two record failures must be escaped. (1) The adaptive HOLD attractor: 887/collapse-confirm (policies that act more lose more, monotone: A −2.86% / E −9.11% / D −13.84%, at fee0), 885 (it is the distillation loop sharpening toward its own visits, not search depth), 849 (value leaf action-blind, v̂ corr +0.03), 892 (OOS actions worse than a matched coin flip, Δ −0.043..−0.056), 812 (greedy policy abstains: policy turnover 0.000, Sharpe nan, `runs/812_mcts_trader/MINIMAL_LOOP_RESULT.md`). Mechanical escape, not hope: (a) the execution episode has a MANDATORY terminal cross at T (Nevmyvaka's formulation; Ning et al. add a ΔT step) — the trade list is exogenous, "do nothing" is not an available fixed point, the only degenerate policy is "always cross immediately", which is a legitimate measured answer (= the taker tier), not a collapse; (b) the reward is realized shortfall observed on every episode within an hour — no self-generated value target, no visit-distribution target, so the 885/887 self-referential sharpening cannot form; (c) the transition is action-dependent (limit offset → queue → fill), so the learned object contains information a policy prior over an exogenous price path never could; (d) the horizon is short enough for exact DP, so there is no learned leaf to be action-blind. (2) The never-validated fill model: 897's lineage assumed OHLC-touch fills + a flat 0/5/10 bp adverse term (`sweep_gated_maker.py:96`; 809 even assumed a maker REBATE of −2..−5 bp, `TASK_809:61`, against Kraken's real 4–25 bp maker fees), 907 exists because it was never validated, and a synthetic simulator (TASK_047 distance-based fill probability; `mcts_trader/exchange/paper.py:31-33` flat 0.1% fee/0.05% slippage; Bella/TASK_110 generate OHLC paths, not queues) reintroduces the same circularity. Escape: learn ONLINE from real micro-notional fills only — the fill is the datum, not a model of the fill; at $5–10 size the agent's own impact is nil, so Nevmyvaka's no-impact factorization holds and no simulator is needed for market variables. Residual that is NOT escaped: fills learned at micro size do not transfer to sizes that are not micro on the thin tail of the 273-asset PIT universe, and 907 covers 4 majors only.

bear_positive_without_forecast.argument: An execution layer inherits the gross book's sign: with a fixed trade list, E[book return] is the parent's forecast and execution only subtracts less. On a book with gross Sharpe ≤ 0 it makes a negative number less negative (−0.18 → ≈ −0.07 at best). Worse, its savings are pro-cyclical: passive buys fill most and are adversely selected most in fast down-moves, and non-fills at the deadline pay taker plus drift, so realized execution cost is highest in exactly the bear regimes where the goalposts demand positivity. The record's only bear-positive behaviour is the trend book's short leg (BEAR22 +1.095 vs long-flat −2.471, LEDGER 898), which is a forecast.

honest_use: A bounded, one-time COST-TIER MEASUREMENT with a controller attached — not an edge row. Legitimate roles: (1) close D65 honestly by replacing the assumed fee16/slip5 with a measured maker-execution cost (fee_maker + realized adverse selection + non-fill×taker) for the operator's actual Kraken tier, so every later book — including whatever passes TASK_915 — is graded at a cost tier that was observed rather than asserted; (2) supply the live-execution module the gate ladder's paper/live rungs need anyway (`deployment_gate_ladder.md`), reusing 907's recorder and phase-2 rails; (3) be the one place in the program where a 'self-learning loop' is posed as a genuinely controlled MDP, so the operator's algorithmic preference gets a clean test whose failure mode is a boring 'always cross' rule, not a HOLD collapse. It must be scheduled AFTER TASK_915's G-A read, never in place of it: if G-A fails everywhere the pre-committed consequence (D79) is a DATA row, and an execution layer on a book with no edge is worth −0.18 → −0.07. Fold into the tactics panel's row 2 as its live half; cap at the two-line rule unless step-1 F3 shows ≥3 bp/side of state-conditional structure.
compute: Tiny and CPU-only. Recorder: already running under safe_run on gpu-server (tmux). Learner: exact DP over ≤(60 steps × 8 inventory levels × 4 actions) with ≤6 discretized market variables, or a ridge/contextual bandit — seconds to minutes on one CPU core, <1 GB RAM. Order engine: one asyncio process, negligible. The only heavy step is reading the 4.1-day capture (14.83 GB peak RSS at cycle 3; TASK_914 streaming reader is queue row 2 and removes it). GPU: none. The 64 GB GPUs buy nothing here. Wall time dominates: 30–60 calendar days of real micro-order collection.

kill_experiment.design: Two steps, both pre-registered, both PAIRED so the price-path noise cancels. STEP 0 (zero money; needs the shipped 907 B2 artifact or a scratch render of the FINAL capture; also needs the operator's ACTUAL Kraken maker/taker pair on record first, because the record disagrees: 'taker16' in POWERED_RESULT.md:7/TASK_808:49 vs attainable MAKER {8,16} in TASK_897:284). For every minute bar × 4 pairs × both sides, compute the paired shortfall of arm P = 'post-only at the touch, deadline T∈{15,30,60} min, fill iff a print trades THROUGH the limit (near-exact for micro size), cross the remainder at T' minus arm M = 'taker at the concurrent touch', fees at the operator's tier. Regress the paired saving on ≤6 state variables (spread ticks, top imbalance, 5-min |ret|/vol, hour, frozen-mid flag, T). STEP 1 (real money, D65 phase 2, operator-armed): ship the `place_order` increment under the existing rails (TASK_910 pins, caps mandatory), then 4 pairs × 2 sides × ~10 slots/day × 30–60 days of real post-only orders at venue minimums, each paired with a virtual taker priced at the concurrent touch (exact at micro size). Record realized fill flag, fill price, mid markouts via the existing shadow engine. Also read the fill rate against 907's touch and through proxies (the D65 deliverable itself).
kill_experiment.instrument: 907 recorder (book depth-10 + trades, venue_ts) + shadow_engine markouts + phase-2 rails; operator's Kraken tier recorded pre-read (gate iv discipline from 897). Statistic: mean paired saving in bp/side with Newey–West SE (lag = T), by pair and T; state-conditional quintile spread with Bonferroni over the state grid. Reported alongside: n, fill rate, non-fill fraction, drift-at-deadline cost. Power: paired shortfall std ≈ 15–25 bp (drift over time-to-fill), so n≈1,200 orders gives SE ≈ 0.5–0.7 bp — 5 bp is detectable at >7σ; the 60-min-window unpaired std (~64 bp on BTC) would need ~3,000/arm, which is why the design is paired.
kill_experiment.pass_fail: KILL THE LOOP (no learner, at most the two-line rule) if EITHER: (K1) unconditional paired saving of P over M < 5 bp/side (CI including 5) at the operator's real tier — then the whole execution family is worth < +0.05 Sharpe on a 0.155/day book and folds into the cost tier as a constant; OR (K2) the best-minus-worst state-quintile spread of the saving is < 3 bp/side or fails NW t≥3 after Bonferroni — then there is no state-conditional surface for a learner to amplify and the rule captures everything. PROCEED to an online learner only if K1 and K2 both fail to kill; its own bar: beat the frozen rule by ≥2 bp/side out-of-sample (later weeks), t≥3, else record the rule as the measured tier and stop. STEP 0 can only KILL (touch/through proxies are optimistic bounds; one week, one regime); STEP 1 is the only pass path. Pre-committed either way: the outcome is a cost-tier update, never a goalposts claim — the ceiling is +0.11 Sharpe and the bar is +0.97.
kill_experiment.cost: STEP 0: CPU hours on the workstation or srv (one 14.8 GB capture read; ~minutes of regression), zero money, ~1 engineer-day after B2 ships. STEP 1: capital at risk ≤ $100 (budget cap; ≤1 open order per pair), fees ≈ $0.01–0.04 per $5–10 order → < $50 total; ~1 engineer-week to ship the real-order increment under the existing rails and its verification panel (the row's real cost — 907 has consumed 4 factory runs on denomination defects); 30–60 calendar days wall time; zero GPU.

honest_odds: P(the design changes ANY goalposts verdict) ≈ 0 — it is bounded by the 0.18 whole-cost-stack Sharpe (POWERED_RESULT), realistically ≤ +0.11 at 21→8 bp, and cannot move the PIT CI off zero or reach +0.97 from a +0.74 gross book. P(a rule-based maker execution saves ≥5 bp/side at the operator's tier, i.e. ≥ +0.05 Sharpe on the trend book) ≈ 50–60%, driven almost entirely by the maker–taker fee gap being real at that tier (the Kraken BTC/USD static-kernel study's 26 → 10.1 bp is the analog). P(a LEARNED policy beats that rule by ≥2–3 bp/side OOS) ≈ 20–30% (literature increments of a few bp are on institutional sizes where impact matters; at micro size the fill surface is mostly 'frozen vs moving mid'). P(the loop produces a conditional-mean signal) = 0 by construction. Conditional on TASK_915 G-A failing everywhere, the value of the loop is negative (it delays the pre-committed data pivot to polish the cost of a book with no edge).
open_doubts: Record inconsistency that decides the fee half of the ceiling: 'fee16 = Kraken taker' (POWERED_RESULT.md:7, TASK_808:49) vs the operator's attainable MAKER set {8,16} bp (TASK_897:284). Under the fetched Kraken ladder a 15–18 bp taker sits at $1M–2.5M/30d where maker is 4–6 bp; a maker of 8–16 bp implies a taker of 20–30 bp, i.e. the record's 21 bp would UNDERSTATE the taker tier. One operator lookup resolves it and should precede any cell being read.

Memo §1.4 states that 5 vs 10 bp adverse selection at daily turnover is '≈0.3–0.5 Sharpe-points/yr of drag'; by the memo's own §1.1 arithmetic (0.1551/day × 365 × 5 bp = 2.8%/yr on a 60–66%-vol book) it is ≈0.04–0.05 Sharpe — about 8× smaller. Not load-bearing for the memo's direction call, but it overstates the execution layer's stake.

Micro-notional fills ($5–10) are the only clean training data yet transfer only in the zero-impact regime; on the thin tail of the 273-asset PIT universe (where most of the 0.155/day turnover lives in 2024–26) queue position and depth matter and 907 covers 4 majors only. The measured tier may be right for BTC/ETH/SOL/XRP and wrong for the book.

The trend book rebalances at the UTC-midnight daily close (trader/data.py aggregation); Kraken spread/depth/frozen-mid regime at that hour is unmeasured — the 907 capture can answer it by hour-of-day bucket.

907's receipt lag 2.4–8.7 s at peak hours (notes_2026-08-30.md:41) is a hard floor on any live policy's reaction time; harmless for a 15–60 min window, fatal for anything faster — so the design must never drift toward minute-scale tactics (897 territory).

The cost model charges target-weight changes only; drift re-trims of the constant-dollar book (tactics panel correction 3, +9–12×/yr uncharged) and hold-shares accounting move the cost stack independently of execution — an execution module changes the ACCOUNTING that grades it, and the two must be pre-registered together.

Adverse selection of resting orders is regime-dependent (worst in fast moves); a 30–60-day window in one regime can calibrate the tier for that regime only — the D65 artifact should be labelled by regime, not read as a constant.

Every paper cited measures RL vs a rule under the paper's OWN fill/impact simulator (Nevmyvaka: no-impact-in-training; Ning: assumed quadratic penalty; Schnaubelt: replay); none reports a live A/B against real fills. The literature's few-bp increments are therefore upper bounds on what a learner adds over a rule, and the Kraken BTC/USD 60% saving came from a static kernel with no learning.

907 B2 has consumed four factory runs on denomination defects (runs 46, 49–51; D78 'last patch round'); the real-order increment this design needs inherits that verification burden and the tree's shared-concurrency hazards — the engineering cost, not the compute, is the real cost.

Schnaubelt 2022 and the Digital Finance 2023 paper were read at abstract/summary level; the Kraken fee page fetched was a localized variant that disagrees with a second schedule in search results — both are flagged, neither is load-bearing beyond 'the maker–taker gap is 10–20 bp/side'.
